newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia central bank will not publish daily rouble band.
newsitem.headline: Russia central bank will not publish daily rouble band.

text.p: Russia's central bank will not announce the 600-point daily corridor for the rouble on the interbank market in 1997, Vladimir Alfyorov, a deputy director of the bank's foreign operations department, said on Tuesday.
He told Reuters no other parameters would be published except the previously announced rouble "crawling peg" for the first and last days of 1997.

In late November the government and central bank said in a joint statement the present currency policy would be kept for 1997, with the rouble easing from 5,500-6,100 per dollar on January, 1, to 5,750-6,350 per dollar on December, 31, 1997.
Rouble fluctuations are currently limited by a 600-point peg which edges down daily two to three points.
The corridor limits were 5,000-5,600 per dollar on July, 1, 5,500-6,100 per dollar on December 31, 1996. The corridor for the whole first half of this year was 4,550-5,150 per dollar.
The central bank also announces daily bid/offer dollar/rouble rates for its currency operations. The midpoint of these rates is the official dollar/rouble rate for the following day.
